'''Jean-Loup Delcroix''' (1924–2003)  was a French physicist, specializing in the physics of gases and plasmas.

==Biography==
Jean-Loup Delcroix received secondary education at [[Lycée Janson-de-Sailly]] in Paris and [[Lycée Champollion]] in [[Grenoble]].<ref name=WhoWho>{{cite web | title=Biographie Jean-Loup Delcroix Universitaire, Chercheur scientifique. | website=Who's Who in France | url=https://www.whoswho.fr/decede/biographie-jean-loup-delcroix_10979 | language=fr }}</ref> He matriculated in 1944 at [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|ENS Paris]] and graduated there in 1948 with outstanding rank in the ''[[agrégation]]'' in physics.<ref name=PTobit>{{cite journal|doi=10.1063/1.1784314|title=Jean-Loup Delcroix |date=2004 |last1=Bers |first1=Abraham |last2=Pointu |first2=Anne-Marie |last3=Bretagne |first3=Jean |journal=Physics Today |volume=57 |issue=7 |page=76 |bibcode=2004PhT....57g..76B |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Picinbono, Bernard|date=January 2004|title=Jean-Loup Delcroix 1924-2003|url=http://www.supelec.fr/actu/JL_Delcroix_14-01-04.pdf|website=supelec.fr}}</ref> He graduated in 1953 with a doctorate from the [[University of Paris]]. His thesis is entitled ''Étude des propriétés statiques des charges d'espace du type magnétron''.<ref>{{cite book|author=Delcroix, Jean-Loup|title=Étude des propriétés statiques des charges d'espace du type magnétron|location=Paris|publisher=Masson|year=1954|url=https://inis.iaea.org/collection/NCLCollectionStore/_Public/48/064/48064467.pdf}}</ref> Under the supervision of [[Yves Rocard]], he participated in the construction and start-up of the linear accelerator at [[Orsay]] from 1952 until 1960.<ref name=PTobit/><ref name=WhoWho/> At [[Paris-Sud University]] he was a ''[[maître de conférences]]'' (MCF) from 1960 to 1965 and a professor from 1965 to 1990, when he retired as professor emeritus.<ref name=WhoWho/> In 1960 Delcroix formed Paris-Sud University's ''Laboratoire de Physique des Gaz et des Plasmas'' (LPGP), in association with the [[CNRS]]. He was the laboratory's director from 1960 to 1984. He made important contributions to the physics of gas discharges and low-temperature plasmas. During the early 1970s he  led a research group on gas discharges with applications to gas laser physics.<ref name=PTobit/>

At Paris-Sud University, Delcroix created in 1960 a graduate curriculum in plasma physics at the level of the [[Master of Advanced Study#France and francophone countries|''diplôme d’études approfondies'' (DEA)]]. His curriculum became a model at other French universities. His lectures on plasma physics formed the basis of three monographs originally published from 1959 to 1966. In 1961 with [[Jean-François Denisse]], he published an important monograph on waves in plasmas.<ref name=PTobit/> Delcroix, in collaboration with Abraham Bers (1930–2015),<ref>{{cite web|title=Abraham Bers, professor emeritus of electrical engineering, dies at 85|website=MIT News|date=September 16, 2015|url=https://news.mit.edu/2015/abraham-bers-professor-emeritus-electrical-engineering-dies-0916}}</ref> wrote a two-volume textbook entitled ''Physique des Plasmas'', published in 1994.<ref name=PTobit/>

From 1965 to 1976 Delcroix was the director of scientific research for the ''Direction des Recherches et Moyens d’Essai'' (D.R.M.E.), France's agency for development and coordination of military research.<ref name=PTobit/> The D.R.M.E. was created in 1961 by Lucien Malavard (1910–1990).<ref>{{cite web|title=La D.R.M.E. a établi un pont entre militaires et scientifiques|author=Vichney, Nicolas|website=Le Monde|date=1965-01-23|language=fr|url=https://www.histcnrs.fr/pdf/DRME.pdf}}</ref> From 1978 to 1989 Delcroix was the Director General of the [[Supélec|École supérieure d'électricité (Supélec)]]. Under his directorship, Supélec expanded to three campuses and modernized its curriculum. From 1982 to 2003 he was France's representative to the [[Committee on Data of the International Science Council|Committee on Data of the International Science Council (CODATA)]].<ref name=PTobit/> Beginning in 1975, Delacroix with several colleagues created and maintained GAPHYOR (GAz PHysique ORsay),<ref name=WhoWho/><ref name=PTobit/> a database and computerized retrieval system for atomic and molecular physics.<ref>{{cite journal|year=1977|author=Delcroix, J. L.|title='GAPHYOR': A computerized retrieval system for the properties of atoms, molecules, gases and plasmas|journal=J. Phys. (Paris), Colloq|issue=3 |url=https://inis.iaea.org/search/search.aspx?orig_q=RN:9358935}}</ref>

The French government appointed him [[Ordre des Palmes académiques|''Chevalier des Palmes académiques'']] (1966), [[Legion of Honour|''Chevalier de la Légion d'honneur'']] (1969), [[Ordre national du Mérite|''Commandeur de l'ordre national du Mérite'']] (1984), and [[Legion of Honour|''Officier de la Legion d'honneur'']] (1989).<ref name=WhoWho/><ref name=PTobit/>

He and his first wife had a son and two daughters. After divorce from his first wife, J.-L. Delcroix remarried and became the stepfather of one child. He was predeceased by his second wife.<ref name=WhoWho/>
